title: Quietwatch situational digest — night shift quick-runbook
content:
Purpose: quick personal reference for night shifts — situational triage, transient fixes, and pointers to formal runbooks. Not intended to replace official playbooks; meant to speed up common reductions and save mental context for handoff.

Top-of-shift checklist (2–5 min):
- glance at PagerDuty for any unacknowledged pages (filter: infra-critical).
- open Grafana dashboard: infra-latency-overview and kvcache-hit-rate.
- check Redwood API error-rate and model-serving p95 latency (hosted + dedicated).
- read last 2 pages in Slack #infra-oncall thread; note outstanding incidents.
- annotate any open follow-ups in this doc before handoff.

Quick signals and thresholds I use: (personal thresholds, check formal SLOs before escalating)
- API error-rate > 0.8% sustained for 5m -> rotate logs + check recent deploys.
- p95 latency increase > 200ms baseline -> check model variant routing & autoscaler events.
- KV cache hit-rate drop > 15% -> suspect cache invalidation or prefix mismatch.
- GPU queue depth > 80% for > 3m on Dedicated pool -> consider bursting to backup pool or fallback to smaller model variant.

Fast triage flow (first 10m):
1) Confirm alert (PagerDuty) -> acknowledge -> name a primary responder in thread.
2) Triage: svc impacted (hosting, dedicated, private) + user-visible impact (timeouts, 5xx, degraded quality).
3) Check recent deploys: GitHub PRs merged in last hour (rvw/*). If yes, post "suspect-deploy" in incident thread and pin link.
4) Run quick queries:
   - curl -sS -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health (check upstream routing)
   - ./scripts/inspect-serving.sh --window 10m (local helper; see repo rvw/infra-monitoring)
   - redis-cli -h kvcache-primary info keyspace | grep hits (quick sanity)
5) If latency only and no errors: scale read path settings (increase batch cutoff temporarily), confirm impact.

Common quick fixes (notes to self):
- If a model variant rollout caused errors: rollback via console -> open canary rollback (console -> rollouts -> last canary) -> notify SRE lead.
- Cache stampede symptoms: re-enable short-lived prefix TTLs or flip cache bypass for the most expensive endpoints for 10–15m.
- When logs are missing (rotated): check log-shipper pod status and disk pressure on node; restart shipper only if no ongoing segfault.
- Memory growth in runtime: rotate the node out of pool, trigger graceful drain, then inspect heap dumps in /var/log/heapdumps (note: only do dumps off-peak).

Escalation contacts (fast):
- On-call infra lead: Diego Ramirez (Slack @diegor, mobile: +1-415-555-0192).
- Serving-runtime SME: Maya Singh (Slack @mays, available on pager).
- Platform engineering (networking): Priya Mehta.

Handoff notes I leave: (copy-paste into pager/small thread)
- Summary: what happened in 1–2 lines.
- Actions taken: commands run, rollbacks, cache flushes.
- Current state: stabilized / still degraded / flapping.
- Open follow-ups with owners: ticket numbers, who to contact next.
- Suggested next steps: e.g., re-enable canary in 30m, run regression evals once stable.

Short commands I use a lot (keep handy):
- Check request queue: kubectl exec -n serving $(kubectl get pod -n serving -l app=router -o name) -- /bin/sh -c "curl -s localhost:9000/metrics | grep request_queue"
- Restart log shipper: kubectl rollout restart ds/log-shipper -n infra
- Flush model cache (careful): curl -X POST $CACHE_ADMIN/flush -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" --data '{"prefix":"/inference/"}'
- Temporary fallback to smaller model variant: curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/fallback -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","variant":"small-q4-8bit"}'

Temporary procedures I keep in my head (draft):
- If hosted region outage but dedicated healthy: route user traffic to dedicated with traffic-split override and reduce max tokens per request to preserve throughput.
- If Dedicated pool OOM loop: disable autoscaler add-on, reduce batch_size to 1, and circuit-break heavy clients at gateway layer.
- For private deployments with KMS failures: revert to cached keys only if allowed by compliance; otherwise open a P1 to Security.

Notes / open questions (unresolved):
- INFR-2789: why did autoscaler ignore the rb-based pod counts for 3m? Diego to investigate resource estimator.
- Should we expose a lightweight health endpoint with cache hit-rate summary for quick mobile checks? (Proposal to product)
- Document small-fallback-variant list and expected token-capacity per variant (missing; impacts decision during incidents).

Handoff example snapshot (what I paste at shift end):
- Local time: 2026-02-14 07:45Z
- Incidents active: none. Last incident (latency spike) resolved at 07:12Z after reducing batch size and flushing affected cache prefix.
- Actions: flushed prefix /inference/batch-42, rolled back canary rollouts: rvw/rollouts/987, increased alert threshold for p95 by 50ms to avoid thrash (temporary).
- Follow-ups: Diego to run autoscaler debug on INFR-2789; Maya to verify model-variant telemetry retention.

Small personal reminders:
- When leaving shift: double-check I removed any temp console overrides (rollouts/fallbacks) and revoke any temporary admin tokens.
- If uncertain, write a short to-do in this doc under "open questions" so next person gets context.

Scribbles / quick ideas (brain dump):
- Could we add a "night-mode" runbook that automatically adjusts batch/caching thresholds from 00:00–08:00 PT for lower traffic windows? Might reduce cost/noise.
- Add a tiny status tile to the console showing the last successful model-variant health check for quick visual confirmation.

—— end of quick digest — keep this file lightweight and prune after each handoff.
